title: Microeconomics Fundamentals
description: Core ideas from an intro microeconomics course: supply and demand, elasticity, surplus, market structures, and market failures.
subject: business-economics

cards.definition: The value of the best alternative you give up when you make a choice.
How strongly quantity demanded responds to a price change: the percent change in quantity divided by the percent change in price.
The total surplus lost when a market produces something other than the efficient quantity, for example because of a tax.
The basic problem that wants exceed the limited resources available, which forces choices about how to use them.
All else equal, when a good's price rises, the quantity demanded falls.
All else equal, when a good's price rises, the quantity supplied rises.
The price at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied, so there is no shortage or surplus.
Quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, usually because the price is below equilibrium.
Quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded, usually because the price is above equilibrium.
A legal maximum price. When set below the equilibrium price, it causes a shortage.
A legal minimum price, such as a minimum wage. When set above the equilibrium price, it causes a surplus.
Quantity demanded changes by a larger percentage than price, so the elasticity's absolute value is greater than 1.
Quantity demanded changes by a smaller percentage than price. Common for necessities with few substitutes.
Goods used in place of each other. A price rise for one increases demand for the other.
Goods used together. A price rise for one decreases demand for the other.
A good whose demand rises when consumers' incomes rise.
A good whose demand falls when consumers' incomes rise.
Each additional unit of a good consumed adds less satisfaction than the one before it.
The difference between what buyers are willing to pay and what they actually pay.
The difference between the price sellers receive and the lowest price they would have accepted.
The additional cost of producing one more unit of output.
The quantity where marginal revenue equals marginal cost.
Many firms sell identical products with free entry and exit, so no single firm can influence the market price.
A single seller of a product with no close substitutes, able to set its price above marginal cost.
A cost or benefit of an activity that falls on third parties who are not part of the transaction, such as pollution.
